now.title: Arm V1 parts
now.note: Buy STS3215 servos and pay the import tax. Keep servo mounts standard so cheaper servos can drop in later.
now.details: Decided 9 Nov: for V1, buy six STS3215 servos (~$16 each retail, ~$10.60 at 1,000+ on Alibaba) in the UK and pay the import tax. Cheaper arms (home-built servos, assembly in Brazil) are an R&D track for V2/V3. Still open: SO-101 ready-made kit versus parts plus printing, once kit prices are checked.

now.title: UK vs Brazil sourcing
now.note: Small, valuable electronics come from the UK in the cabin bag; bulky, generic parts are bought in Brazil.
now.details: Brazilian import tax can roughly double the price of electronics, so the servos, driver board, USB cable and a power supply that works on Brazil voltage go in the cabin bag. The pipe, tank, plywood, filament, N20 motors and the Bambu A1 printer are bought in Brazil. Duty-free allowance is US$1,000 by air; keep receipts.
